Africa covers approximately 30 million square kilometres and is the world’s second-largest continent by both land area and population.



However, advocates say conventional Mercator maps have historically presented the continent visually as considerably less imposing than it is in reality.

The vote enjoyed an overwhelming majority of UN members endorsing the continent’s demand for more accurate global geographical representation.



Togo led negotiations on behalf of the African Group, building on an AU-supported initiative to ensure Africa is no longer represented as smaller than it actually is.

Togolese Foreign Minister Robert Dussey told the UN General Assembly that maps were not merely technical illustrations but powerful instruments influencing how people understand the world.

“Maps shape our understanding of the world. They guide education, nourish the imagination and influence collective perceptions,” Dussey said.



The resolution promotes wider use of the Equal Earth projection and other equal-area maps where accurate comparison of the relative sizes of continents and countries is important.

It describes the consequences as contributing to the “symbolic minimisation” of Africa and other regions in the global collective imagination.



“A fair map does not change the geography of the world; it changes how we see the world,” said, adding, “a fair world begins with a fair map.”

The Equal Earth projection, developed in 2018, seeks to preserve the relative areas of countries and continents, thereby presenting Africa at a much closer-to-actual scale.



Unlike Mercator projections, equal-area projections do not enlarge Africa; rather, they remove the artificial enlargement given to territories near the poles.

The United States strongly rejected the initiative, arguing that the General Assembly should focus on more pressing global challenges.



France, however, supported the resolution, announcing plans to move away from Mercator in its official world maps.

This would also make France, the United States, Russia and other northern countries appear smaller relative to equatorial countries than on the familiar Mercator map.

World.title: US Military Destroys Three Iranian Oil Tankers After Missile Attacks
World.content:
•Iran vows more severe reprisals if attacks continue

The United States military yesterday said its forces struck and disabled three Iranian crude oil tankers after the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) launched ballistic missiles toward two US Navy warships in regional waters.

But the Iranian military in a swift response, has vowed “more severe” retaliatory attacks on US naval vessels if Washington kept up its strikes on Iranian ships.

In a statement shared on US social media company X, CENTCOM said an aircraft carrier and a guided-missile destroyer successfully evaded multiple Iranian attacks, adding that no American personnel were injured.

According to the statement, US forces permanently disabled the M/T Downy off the coast of Kharg Island and the M/T Stark 1 near Jask. They also destroyed the unladen M/T Kylo, also known as the “Noxen,” in the Gulf of Oman after its crew was ordered to abandon ship.

CENTCOM said the vessels were part of a “multibillion-dollar shadow network” allegedly used to finance the IRGC and its regional proxies.

“Let the message to the IRGC be clear: If you shoot at two of our ships, we will impose an even higher economic cost — taking out three of yours,” CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper said.

“We will not hesitate to defend American forces, and if necessary, destroy Iran’s limited and exposed oil fleet,” he added.

Regional tensions have escalated since US-Israeli attacks on Iran began on February 28, with Tehran responding with missile and drone strikes against Israel and US interests across the region.

Washington and Tehran signed a memorandum of understanding on June 18 concerning freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz. Still, its implementation has stalled amid disagreements over security arrangements in the strait.

Meanwhile, Iran’s military has vowed retaliatory attacks on US naval vessels if Washington kept up its strikes on Iranian ships.

It also warned that if the insecurity and harassment of its ships and the naval blockade continue, its strikes on US military vessels in the region would be more severe than before.

“The US terrorist army is warned that if the evil actions, insecurity and harassment of Iranian ships and the naval blockade of Iran continue, the strikes by the armed forces of the Islamic Republic of Iran against US military vessels in the region will be more severe than before and there is a possibility of their expansion,” the Khatam al-Anbiya central command said.

World.title: Atiku Playing to the Gallery, 15 Northern States will Collapse If Subsidy Returns, Don Warns
World.content:
A professor at Obafemi Awolowo University (OAU), Tunji Ogunyemi, has warned that restoring petrol subsidy could leave about 15 states in northern Nigeria unable to sustain their operations within three months.

Ogunyemi gave the warning during an interview on Open Forum 360 on Friday, a podcast hosted by Dare Adekanmbi, while reacting to a proposal by African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, to restore petrol subsidy if elected in 2027.

The professor argued that bringing back the subsidy would reduce the funds available for distribution through the Federation Account, on which most states rely to finance government operations.

“I think it is calamitous, to say the least, if we reverse the subsidy regime in Nigeria in favour of returning the subsidies,” he said.

Ogunyemi said the consequences would extend beyond the states, listing reduced Federation Account revenue as one of four major problems that would arise from a return to the subsidy regime.

“The Federation Account is the jugular of more than 30 states in the federation. Only about four states in Nigeria can survive without the Federation Account,” Ogunyemi stated.

He identified Lagos, Delta and Rivers as states that could cope without depending heavily on federal allocations, while citing Taraba as an example of a state whose finances are significantly dependent on the Federation Account.

“So if you now say reduce the accrual from the account, I tell you more than about 15 states in the north will collapse. They will collapse within three months,” he stated.

He added that a revenue squeeze would make it difficult for state governments to meet their obligations to workers and pensioners.

He said, “The second is that states will return to a regime of incapacity to pay salaries, let alone pensions.”

Ogunyemi also warned that the federal government would face difficulties funding its recurrent and capital expenditure if its revenue share declined.

He said between 60 and 70 per cent of the federal government’s expenditure goes to recurrent spending, describing it as “consumption expenditure”.

“That is consumption expenditure. You reduce the revenue in that respect, you will see a situation in which government will not be able to support its minimum expenditure, let alone go for capital expenditure,” he said.

The professor further warned that declining revenues could affect the country’s ability to service its debts.

According to Ogunyemi, failure to meet those obligations could damage Nigeria’s financial standing and creditworthiness.

He also questioned Atiku’s proposal, suggesting that the former vice president could be using the subsidy promise to gain political support.

He argued that Atiku, having served as vice-president, should be more explicit about the possible consequences of restoring the subsidy.

Atiku had initially pledged to restore the subsidy, arguing that Nigerians had not seen sufficient benefits from its removal and questioning how the funds saved from the policy had been used.

However, Atiku later clarified that his proposal was not a return to the former import-subsidy arrangement. He said he favoured a targeted and capped intervention that would support domestic refining and production, with transparency and auditing built into the scheme.

The subsidy was removed by President Bola Tinubu during his inauguration on May 29, 2023, when he declared that “fuel subsidy is gone.”

The policy immediately triggered a sharp increase in petrol prices and contributed to higher transportation and living costs.

The federal government has defended the decision as necessary to reduce fiscal pressure and free resources for other levels of government.

The finance ministry said the reforms generated an estimated N15.8tn in resources for the federation between June 2023 and December 2025.

World.title: FG: Tinubu’s Reforms Have Achieved a Reasonable Degree of Price Stability and Economic Growth
World.content:
Segun Awofadeji in Bauchi



The federal government has said President Bola Tinubu’s reforms have achieved a reasonable degree of price stability and economic growth, adding that the country was gradually moving towards economic and social stability.

The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Sola Enikanolaiye, stated this yesterday while speaking with journalists on the sidelines of a sensitisation workshop on the ECOWAS Trade Liberalisation Scheme for the North-east geopolitical zone, held in Bauchi State.



The workshop, with the theme, “Increasing Intra-Regional Trade Through ECOWAS Trade Liberalisation Scheme,” was organised by the ECOWAS National Unit of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in collaboration with the Bauchi State Government.

Enikanolaiye said the programme was part of efforts to bring Nigeria’s foreign policy closer to the people and create economic opportunities for businesses, entrepreneurs and other stakeholders.



He said, “One of the main reasons we decided to organise this workshop is in line with our 4D foreign policy framework, which places the Nigerian people at the centre of our foreign policy.

“We are looking at ways and means of bringing foreign policy closer to Nigerians at the grassroots in a manner that enhances their prosperity and expands economic opportunities within the West African region.”



According to him, the workshop was designed to encourage Nigerian businesses, including small and medium-sized enterprises, large-scale companies and agricultural enterprises, to explore opportunities within the West African sub-region and the wider African market.



He said the sensitisation programme would be held across the six geopolitical zones before concluding in Abuja.

Speaking on the state of the Nigerian economy, the minister said the economic reforms of President Tinubu’s administration had contributed to greater stability and growth.



He said, “Price fluctuations are a function of the macroeconomic and microeconomic policies of every country, but I can only speak for Nigeria on this occasion.

“I can say, without fear of contradiction, that the economic reforms of President Bola Tinubu have achieved a great degree of stabilisation and growth.



“You cannot promote economic development without growth. If your economy is suffering from zero or negative growth, there is no way we can talk about the benefits of development.

“So, we have attained that stage, and we are moving progressively towards economic development, social development and prosperity,” he added.



The minister acknowledged that inflation remained high but said it was declining, adding that other economic indicators were showing signs of improvement.

In his remarks, Bauchi State Governor, Bala Mohammed, said the state government was committed to supporting local investments and expanding opportunities for businesses.



The governor, who his deputy, Auwal Jatau, represented, said the ECOWAS Trade Liberalisation Scheme was aimed at facilitating legitimate trade in qualifying products originating within the ECOWAS region, promoting investment, expanding markets, strengthening production and deepening economic cooperation among member states.



The governor also called for stronger economic cooperation among the North-east states, noting that the region possessed complementary economic strengths.

World.title: Julius Malema promises to increase SASSA old-age grant to R4 500
World.content:
Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) leader Julius Malema has promised to increase the South African Social Security Agency (SASSA) old-age grant to R4 500 per month if his party comes to power.

Malema made the promise while addressing EFF supporters at the party’s provincial manifesto launch in North West on Saturday, as political parties campaign ahead of the 4 November local government elections.

JULIUS MALEMA PRIOMISES R4500 OLD-AGE GRANT

During his address, Malema assured beneficiaries that an EFF-led government would not remove social grants, accusing the African National Congress (ANC) of failing to adequately support pensioners.



“You paid taxes while you were working, that is your money. We will not take away your grants, instead we will double them. In fact, we want it to start at R4 500,” he said.

South Africa’s old-age grant is currently R2 400 per month following an R80 increase announced in the 2026 Budget. Beneficiaries aged over 75 receive R2 420.

Malema also criticised the R370 Social Relief of Distress (SRD) grant, saying it was insufficient to meet the needs of unemployed South Africans. He called for the introduction of a grant for unemployed graduates.

The SRD grant currently remains at R370 per month, with government having allocated funding for it to continue until 31 March 2027.

‘GOVERNMENT CAN AFFORD THE INCREASE’

Julius Malema repeated the R4 500 proposal during an address in Mpumalanga on the same day, saying pensioners deserved the increase because many of them support their families financially.

“They will be able to look after us and look after our children. They deserve better, we must support them and we must fight for them because fighting for Gogo’s is fighting for black families. They are the heads of black families,” he said.



Malema argued that the government could afford to increase the grant if public funds were not being misused.

WATCH🚨



EFF leader Julius Malema has called for the old-age grant to be increased to R4,500 a month, saying pensioners, particularly grandmothers, are the backbone of black families and that government can afford the increase if it stops misusing public funds. pic.twitter.com/EKxdmPVtYk — MDN NEWS (@MDNnewss) September 5, 2026

The proposal comes as political parties campaign ahead of the local government elections, with social grants, unemployment and the cost of living expected to remain key issues among voters.

The EFF has previously campaigned on substantially increasing social grants. Its 2019 manifesto, for example, proposed increasing the grant for older persons from R1 700 to R3 400 per month.

World.title: Updated rugby rankings: Springboks win, Wallabies-Argentina draw
World.content:
The Springboks featured in their final home Test of the year on Saturday, and ultimately claimed an impressive 29-24 win over the All Blacks at the FNB Stadium, a result which saw Rassie Erasmus’ team improve their handy buffer at the top of the World Rugby rankings.

The 29-24 victory also gave the Springboks a 2-1 lead in Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series, with one test remaining in Baltimore, USA on Saturday.

As a result of the deserved win, the Springboks received another 0.95 rankings points, and South Africa now hold a 2.43 lead at the summit of the standings.



Meanwhile, Argentina and the Wallabies played out a high-scoring draw in the second leg of their standalone two-Test series. Australia had won the first Test 27–21 in San Juan the previous weekend.

The draw hasn’t had much of an impact on the rankings as Australia hold onto seventh spot.

In one other game to note, Japan celebrated the 100th anniversary of the Japan Rugby Football Union with a dominant nine-try victory over Canada.

Both the Springboks and All Blacks will now share a flight to the USA to prepare for the final match on Saturday night in a tour that has lived up to its branding as “Like no Other”.

Erasmus said: “Hopefully me and Dave (Rennie, All Blacks head coach) will have a beer. His will be a little bit more bitter and mine will be a little sweeter. But then on Sunday we arrive there and we get into camp again.



“We assess the injuries; we start planning and it’s number one and two again. It’s the greatest rivalry and we play to try and win the series, and they will try and to draw the series. So, no, it’s going to be flipping important.”

World.title: Find out entrance fees as The Cradle Berry Farm reopens!
World.content:
The beloved Cradle Berry Farm in Muldersdrift, Johannesburg, officially reopened on 5 September 2026, after closing in December 2025.

Depending on the weather conditions, the farm will remain open until December 2026, giving visitors ample time to plan a sweet escape to the farm.

THE CRADLE BERRY FARM REOPENS FOR 2026

The farm operates between 8:00 AM and 5:00 PM on Saturdays, Sundays, and public holidays. The entrance fee is R100 for adults, R70 for kids, plus R100 per kg for takeaway berries.



However, there’s more to this farm than just picking and munching on fresh strawberries. Visitors can also host special events such as weddings and parties, or enjoy a picnic experience where they can either bring their own food or order delicious meals from the in-house café, J-Mo’s.

Homemade juices, preserves, and small batches of jam are also available at the farm, made with only natural ingredients.



Due to the rain and cold weather on 6 September, visitors are advised to wear raincoats and boots, and to bring umbrellas, which are essential for strawberry picking in the fields.

The exciting opening weekend also includes the “Funky Hat Competition,” where visitors can wear their “craziest hats” or even create one right at the farm. The “wildest creation” will walk away with a fresh strawberry hamper.

World.title: Fate of October 2026 SASSA Grant top-ups still TBD
World.content:
Affected beneficiaries await confirmation on October 2026 SASSA Grant top-ups from the agency. Image: File

October 2026 SASSA Grant top-ups are still to be decided for millions of ‘core’ social-welfare beneficiaries.

However, in typical government fashion, the usual date of confirmation – the Medium-Term Budget Policy Statement (MTBPS) – falls after next months’ disbursement dates.

This is not the first time the National Treasury and agency have had their lines crossed over grant increases.



Last year, in the wake of Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana’s failed attempt to increase VAT, above inflation SASSA Grant increases were pushed through.

However, three consecutive budgets were rejected by mid-year, at which time reversing April increases retroactively was impossible.

OCTOBER 2026 SASSA GRANT TOP-UPS

Will the new minister be able to argue for October 2026 SASSA Grant top-ups with the National Treasury in the coming weeks? Image: File

As a result, it’s like the South African Social Security Agency has been paying the price ever since.



The Treasury’s 2026 Budget seemed to settle the discussion back in February.

From 1 April 2026, Older Person, Disability and Care Dependency all increased to R2 400. While War Veterans and over 75s went up to R2 420.

Likewise, Child Support climbed R20 to R580. And that’s where they’ve sat with no official confirmation on October 2026 SASSA Grant top-ups since …



Meanwhile, this is a genuine shift from how 2024 and 2025 worked.

For two years running, several ‘core’ grants got a smaller top-up in October.

Granted, it was only R10, but every cent counts for recipients struggling to make ends meet each month. Many of the country’s elderly have been marching to parliament demanding R5 000 per month state pensions …



AT LEAST ONE FOR OCTOBER 2026 SASSA GRANT TOP-UPS

However, there is some sliver of hope.

That is the one exception we could find in the Treasury’s Budget Review document.

It says quite clearly that SASSA Foster Care is scheduled for a R10 bump from R1 290 to R1 300 in October 2026. And while that only applies to a few thousand court-appointed Childcare beneficiaries it does suggest the agency isn’t opposed to top-ups before the end of the year.



Civil society groups believe the absence of October 2026 SASSA Grant top-ups for core beneficiaries has to do with the R370 Social Relief of Distress (SRD).

Back in his February Budget briefing, Minister Godongwana said the ‘expanded’ SRD grant would finally be revealed in the MTBPS.

In its current form, the ‘temporary’ grant lives on until 31 March 2027. At which point it’s understood that the next phase will kick-in, with government committing an extra R36.4 billion to the pot.



Top-ups or not, the dates below are the ones you must mark in your diary for next month. Image: File

Here’s a reminder of all SASSA payment dates next month, roughly four weeks’ away from the date of publishing:

Older Person: Friday, 2 October 2026

Disability Grant: Monday, 5 October 2026

Childcare: Tuesday, 6 October 2026

Fourth payment date following grant review: Wednesday, 7 October 2026

SRD R370: Batches from 26 to 31 October 2026

For further information you can contact the agency here:

Toll-free: 0800 60 10 11

Website: www.sassa.gov.za

SRD status checks: srd.sassa.gov.za

Of course, nothing here is final until Finance Minister Godongwana reveals more in Wednesday 21 October’s MTBPS.



Likewise, the agency might still conceivably announce October 2026 SASSA Grant top-ups in the intervening weeks. At which point we will update you.

But what do you think? Do you think we’re likely to see increases next month? Does it even matter when the numbers are so low? Please share your thoughts in the comments section below …

World.title: What R5 000 buys in Botswana vs South Africa
World.content:
Where does R5 000 stretch further — Botswana or South Africa? Image: Pexels

With grocery prices continuing to squeeze household budgets, shoppers are increasingly looking for ways to make their money stretch further.

In South Africa, the average household food basket tracked by the Pietermaritzburg Economic Justice and Dignity Group has remained above R5 000, highlighting the pressure facing consumers.

But what happens when you take the same R5 000 across the border to Botswana?



We compared the prices of nine everyday grocery items in Botswana and South Africa to see how far the money goes.

For the Botswana comparison, we used a SPAR promotion running until 6 September 2026, while South African prices were taken from Shoprite promotions and current price listings available during the same period.

Botswana prices were converted into rand using an exchange rate of P1 = R1.192619 on 5 September 2026.



What groceries cost in Botswana vs South Africa

Grocery item Botswana Botswana in rands South Africa 10kg maize meal P62.99 R75.14 R69.99 10kg rice P119.99 R143.11 R129.99 2L cooking oil P59.99 R71.53 R69.99 6 x 1L long-life milk P131.99 R157.37 R99.99 5kg flour P61.99 R73.92 R79.99 2kg chicken portions P72.99 R87.05 R99.98* 500g pasta P13.99 R16.68 R19.99 5kg brown sugar P78.99 R94.21 R112.48 400g pilchards P30.99 R36.95 R22.99

South Africa’s chicken figure is based on a whole-chicken price of R49.99 per kilogram rather than an identical 2kg frozen-portions pack, so it should be treated as an indicative comparison.

The Botswana SPAR promotion lists 10kg Chobe Super Special maize meal at P62.99, 10kg Spekko rice at P119.99, 2L SPAR sunflower oil at P59.99, six litres of long-life milk at P131.99, 5kg SPAR white bread flour at P61.99 and 2kg frozen chicken portions at P72.99. It also lists Fatti’s & Moni’s 500g pasta at P13.99, 5kg sugar at P78.99 and 400g Lucky Star pilchards at P30.99. The promotion was valid through 6 September 2026 at selected SPAR stores.

In South Africa, Shoprite’s promotions for the period included Ritebrand 10kg maize meal at R69.99 and Spekko 10kg rice at R129.99. The same Shoprite promotions also listed Excella 2L sunflower oil at R69.99.



Shoprite’s current price listings also show Fatti’s & Moni’s 500g pasta at R19.99, while a 2kg pack of Selati Golden Brown Sugar was advertised at R44.99 and 400g Ritebrand pilchards at R22.99.

Botswana is not cheaper across the board

The comparison produces an interesting result.

Botswana comes out cheaper on flour, chicken, pasta and sugar among the selected products.



For example, 5kg of SPAR white bread flour costs P61.99, equivalent to about R73.92. A comparable 5kg bag of Sasko cake wheat flour at Shoprite is listed at R79.99.

The difference is even more noticeable for sugar. The Botswana SPAR promotion lists 5kg of refined white or brown sugar at P78.99, or about R94.21.

In South Africa, Shoprite’s 2kg Selati Golden Brown Sugar is R44.99, meaning 5kg at that rate would cost approximately R112.48.



Pasta is another area where Botswana has an advantage.

A 500g pack of Fatti’s & Moni’s costs P13.99 in the Botswana promotion, compared with R19.99 for the same size in South Africa.

South Africa wins on some staples

The picture changes when looking at some of the biggest grocery staples.



A 10kg bag of maize meal costs P62.99 in Botswana, equivalent to approximately R75.14.

The Shoprite promotion has Ritebrand 10kg maize meal at R69.99, giving South African shoppers a saving of about R5 compared with the converted Botswana price.

Rice also favours South Africa in this comparison.



The Botswana SPAR promotion lists 10kg of Spekko rice at P119.99, or about R143.11. The equivalent 10kg Spekko promotion at Shoprite is R129.99.

Cooking oil is almost evenly matched. Botswana’s 2L SPAR sunflower oil works out at approximately R71.53, compared with R69.99 for 2L Excella sunflower oil at Shoprite.

The biggest difference in the selected basket is milk.



Six litres of SPAR long-life full-cream milk costs P131.99, equivalent to about R157.37.

A current Shoprite listing for six 1L cartons of Crystal Valley UHT full-cream long-life milk shows R99.99, making South Africa considerably cheaper on this product.

So where does R5 000 go further?

Adding the nine selected products gives a Botswana total of P633.91.



At the exchange rate used in this comparison, that works out to approximately R756.01.

The equivalent South African basket comes to approximately R637.90.

That means the selected basket is about R118 more expensive in Botswana after converting the prices into rand.



Put another way, if a shopper repeatedly bought this particular nine-item basket, R5 000 would cover about six full baskets in Botswana, with money left over, compared with about seven baskets in South Africa.

But this is not evidence that South Africa is universally cheaper.

The comparison is based on a limited selection of products and advertised specials. Prices vary between supermarkets, stores, regions and promotions.



Prices are based on advertised promotions and current price listings available around 5–6 September 2026. Botswana prices were converted to rand at P1 = R1.192619. Prices may vary by store, location, availability and loyalty-card requirements.

World.title: All Blacks captain scoffs at claims South Africa is ‘dangerous’
World.content:
Ardie Savea is full of praise for South Africa. Images via X

All Blacks captain Ardie Savea has brushed off claims that South Africa is a “dangerous” country.

The New Zealand national team has been in the country for the past month as part of the Greatest Rivalry series.

Their final game in SA took place at the FNB Stadium, where they lost to the Springboks 29-24. The rugby rivals’ fourth and final fixture will take place in Baltimore, Maryland.



ARDIE SAVEA REJECTS CLAIM SA IS ‘DANGEROUS’ COUNTRY

Speaking at a media briefing ahead of their clash against the Springboks at FNB Stadium on Saturday, Ardie Savea touched on the Greatest Rivalry series, his friendship with Siya Kolisi and his teammates.

The All Blacks captain was also asked about his experience in South Africa, particularly from a safety standpoint. Ardie’s wife, Saskia and their three children joined the team during their trip to SA.

He responded: “It’s been amazing to be in a country like South Africa. They say, ‘You’ve got to be careful, it’s dangerous’, yeah, there may be parts of Africa that are dangerous. But the majority of the time that they’ve been here has been absolutely beautiful.



He continued: “They’ve had an awesome time, the people, the people are amazing. For me to do my work with the All Blacks and come and see them [afterwards], it’s been a massive blessing”.

“South Africa’s dangerous? Our family’s had a beautiful time.” – Ardie Savea on his time in South Africa pic.twitter.com/uvhaF35C96 — Forever Sports (@ForeverSportsOn) September 5, 2026

On his off days, Ardie has joined Saskia and their children by visiting various tourist hotspots around the country.



Ardie has also had quality time with local All Blacks supporters, enjoyed local cuisine and even visited one fan’s home!

END OF THE ROAD FOR THE GREATEST RIVALRY SERIES

Meanwhile, Ardie Savea will not be joining the All Blacks for their last Greatest Rivalry match against the Springboks, set to take place in the US.

The 32-year-old sustained a shoulder injury in the first half of the match.



The fourth and final game will mark the first time the rugby rivals will play each other in America.

It’s unclear who will helm the team as captain.

World.title: ‘Whitney’ singer wows at final Springbok home game [video]
World.content:
Belinda Davids performs the national anthem at the FNB Stadium. Images via X

Belinda Davids, who has built a career as a Whitney Houston tribute singer, performed another unforgettable national anthem at the FNB Stadium, where the Springboks played the All Blacks in the Greatest Rivalry series.

The talented performer – who once brought Britain’s Got Talent judge Simon Cowell to tears – sang at the final Boks test match for the year.

South Africa beat their New Zealand rivals 29-24. The fourth and final match will take place in Baltimore, Maryland, next weekend.



BELINDA DAVIDS WOWS WITH NATIONAL ANTHEM

Not for the first time, Belinda Davids was given the privilege of singing the national anthem for the Springboks.

The Gqeberha-born singer wore a bewelled gown in the colours of the South African flag as she belted out Nkosi Sikelel iAfrika in front of the crowd at the 96 000 seater FNB Stadium.

The performance was enough to make Springbok Deon Fourie weep!



Watch it below…

A riveting rendition of South Africa's national anthem at FNB Stadium 🥹❤️

Belinda last sang the national anthem for the Springboks’ match against Italy in Gqeberha, her hometown, last year.



Speaking ahead of the game, the singer told Daily Maverick: “You have no idea how exciting this is for me. Because I get to do it at home, what an honour. And it’s long overdue, to be honest. I can’t wait!”

THE GREATEST LOVE

Belinda Davids is well known for headlining the Whitney Houston tribute concert, The Greatest Love of All, across South Africa and around the world.

The talented star performs Whitney’s hit songs, such as I Will Always Love You, I Wanna Dance With Somebody, and I’m Every Woman amongst others, in the two-hour production.



In 2017, Belinda won the BBC1 talent competition Even Better Than the Real Thing, performing as a Whitney Houston tribute artist.

Two years later, she received the special recognition award from the UK National Tribute Music Awards for her “global contribution to tribute performing”.

Belinda Davids has previously sang the national anthem for the Springboks.

Images via Facebook

In 2020, Belinda moved Britain’s Got Talent judge Simon Cowell to tears during her audition, which blew up on social media. In 2023, she returned for the All-Star season, where she earned a Golden Buzzer pass.



Belinda comes from a family of seven children and grew up singing gospel in church.

Inspired by Whitney herself, she began performing professionally at just 14.

World.title: Six years later, ‘Lord Kambala’ still haunts Kaizer Chiefs
World.content:
It has been exactly six years since Manuel Kambala scored the header that broke the hearts of Kaizer Chiefs supporters and handed Mamelodi Sundowns the 2019/20 league title.

Needing a victory against Baroka FC in the final match of the season, Amakhosi were held to a 1-1 draw, surrendering the title to Sundowns by just two points.

Chiefs had appeared to be cruising towards the championship after building a commanding 13-point lead earlier in the season. However, a dramatic collapse in the final stages allowed Sundowns to claw their way back into contention.



Then came that fateful moment which broke the hearts of millions of Amakhosi fans.

Kambala rose highest to head Baroka level, denying Chiefs the victory they desperately needed and effectively ending their title hopes.

Six years later, the Mozambican midfielder remains a cult hero among Sundowns and Orlando Pirates supporters.

Kambala broke the hearts of Chiefs supporters that day

On Saturday, supporters once again celebrated Kambala and the famous header that changed the title race forever. His popularity among rival supporters has even earned him the unforgettable nickname: Lord Kambala.

In an interview with KickOff in 2023, Kambala admitted that he appreciated the attention, although he sometimes wished people would remember him for more than that one moment.

“The supporters. They gave me ‘Lord Kambala’ because of what happened in that game against Kaizer Chiefs in 2020.



“I don’t know if it’s Chiefs supporters, Sundowns supporters or even Pirates supporters.”

Kambala also revealed that his popularity exploded after the goal.

“Since that day I’ve been receiving more friend requests and gaining more followers on social media. But I can’t tell if these are my fans or football supporters.”

Asked whether he enjoyed the nickname and the attention that came with it, Kambala gave a rather honest response.

“Sometimes yes and sometimes no. I meet a lot of people who remind me of that goal. I don’t know if it’s a good thing or not.

“There are those who remind me because of what I do in the field of play, and not because I scored against Kaizer Chiefs,” Kambala added.

For Kambala, however, there was nothing extraordinary about what he did that day. He was simply doing his job.

“Those who understand football understand that I was doing my job. It was either them or us. Baroka was fighting for survival that day. Otherwise, they would have been relegated.

“Maybe Kaizer Chiefs as a big team they should have done better than they did that day. They had quality players.”

Despite his attempts to move beyond the moment, the legacy of that header continues to follow him.

“Everyone here calls me Lord Kambala,” said the Kaizer Chiefs slayer.

Was this the darkest moment in Chiefs’ history?

World.title: Diddy to leave prison earlier than expected
World.content:
NEW JERSEY - Sean 'Diddy' Combs could be released from prison sooner than expected.

The former rapper and music mogul’s release date has been moved up to 5 February 2028, according to US Federal Bureau of Prisons records.

Combs is serving a 50-month sentence after being convicted on two counts of transporting people across state lines for prostitution.

He was acquitted of the more serious charges of sex trafficking and racketeering conspiracy.

Prosecutors accused him of using violence, threats and coercion in connection with sexual encounters.

Combs denied the allegations and is appealing his conviction and sentence.

World.title: ‘Bring back fuel levy relief’ - COSATU
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - COSATU is calling for government to bring back fuel levy relief as soaring prices put households under even more pressure.

Petrol has jumped by over R1 a litre while diesel is up by more than R3.

The federation’s Zanele Sabela said previous fuel levy relief helped protect both workers and the economy.

"For COSATU, what had happened earlier this year with the fuel price relief, where governments suspended a portion of the fuel levy was actually the way to go, because it not only protected the working class and the poor, but it also protected the economy.

“And so, this is what we're calling for once again, as we see prices continuing to increase. And so that is what we have seen, because we all know that once the price of fuel goes up, it tends to have a trickle-down effect and actually impacts on all other prices.

“This is what we're calling for. We're calling for that relief to come through again, because people are just not coping. I mean, people who earn the lowest, they spend up to 40% of their salaries on transport to go and to come back from work. And so obviously, when you look at that, that is not sustainable. "

World.title: Argentina ordered to return Nazi-looted painting to Jewish collector's heir
World.content:
BUENOS AIRES - Argentina is set to return an 18th-century painting stolen by Nazis from a Dutch Jewish art collector to the rightful owner's heir, a judge said Friday.

"Portrait of a Lady" by Italian late baroque painter Giacomo Ceruti was missing for eight decades before being photographed last year hanging in the home of the daughter of a senior Nazi officer, who had fled to Argentina after World War II.

"An order will be issued for the painting to be returned to the heir" of art dealer Jacques Goudstikker, judge Santiago Inchausti declared following an agreement reached between the concerned parties.

The painting was first recognized by the Dutch newspaper AD in photographs of a house for sale in the seaside resort of Mar del Plata.

It was hanging above a green sofa in the living room of Patricia Kadgien, whose father Friedrich Kadgien was a financier for the Nazi SS paramilitary organization.

He was one of several high-ranking Nazis to escape to Argentina after World War II.

Patricia Kadgien, who clutched a rosary during the hearing in Mar del Plata, was charged with concealment and placed under house arrest along with her husband when the artwork was identified.

The pair agreed to return the painting to Goudstikker's daughter-in-law and sole heir Marei von Saher and give around $3,200 to local hospitals.

"The individuals under investigation essentially committed themselves to renouncing any rights over the painting that is going to be returned," federal prosecutor Carlos Martinez told AFP.

The work "is in good condition, and expert examinations confirmed its authenticity," Martinez said.

- Going on display -

"Portrait of a Lady" was among over 1,000 artworks stolen from Goudstikker's collection after the Nazi invasion of the Netherlands in 1940.

Goudstikker fled his country days after the invasion, leaving behind a litany of works that were divvied up by top German officials.

After the war, the Dutch state retrieved some 300 works from the collection, most of which it later returned to Goudstikker's heirs.

But more remain scattered around the globe.

The painting in question is by Ceruti (1698-1767), known as "Il Pitocchetto," and not the portraitist Giuseppe Ghislandi as initially reported, the Argentine government stated in a press release.

The work is currently under the care of Argentina's Supreme Court, and it is now up to Von Saher's legal team to initiate its return to its owner.

Von Saher intends to display the painting in Argentina as a way to give visibility to Goudstikker's story.

"The family's intention is for it to be exhibited in Buenos Aires for at least a year," her lawyer Guillermo Brady told AFP, adding that his client is in talks with several museums to iron out the details.

World.title: Beer industry warns excise tax overhaul could cost jobs
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The beer industry is frothing over Treasury’s proposed overhaul of alcohol excise taxes.

It warns the changes could threaten jobs and fuel the illicit alcohol trade.

SA Breweries said government must look beyond tax increases and consider the impact on consumers and the legal market.

SAB’s Fatsani Banda said there needs to be greater tax certainty, with excise taxes coming in line with inflation.

“We are concerned about some of the proposals that National Treasury has put on the table. In particular, what has been proposed is a 20% increase in the rate of standard beer, and that would essentially increase the price gap that already exists between illicit alcohol and legal alcohol.

“We're also concerned by the proposal around tax certainty, which encourages an up to 10% increase in excise taxes every single year in a macroeconomic environment where consumers are cash strapped and are still facing growing concerns around inflation.

“So we do think the proposals in the current consultation process need to be reviewed in light of a multiplicity of factors, which SAB thinks needs to be due consideration throughout the development of this new excise policy framework."

World.title: Severe weather warnings issued for several provinces
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - South Africans are urged to take precautions as severe weather may affect several provinces from tonight.

The South African Weather Service has issued an Orange Level 5 warning for heavy rain, severe thunderstorms, damaging winds and possible flooding affecting parts of the Northern Cape and Gauteng.

“Such conditions could result in localised flooding, damaging winds and hail, and pose a risk to community safety. Please be alert and take necessary precautions,” the weather service said in a statement.

A Level 4 warning is also in place for the Free State, KwaZulu-Natal and North West with damaging winds predicted for the Western Cape.

Emergency services and traffic authorities are monitoring conditions.

The public is advised to avoid unnecessary travel, stay indoors during thunderstorms and never attempt to cross flooded roads or fast-flowing water.

World.title: Will former speaker walk due to lack of evidence?
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Former National Assembly Speaker Nosiviwe Mapisa-Nqakula is waiting for judgment on her discharge application.

Her defence argued that the state had failed to present enough evidence for the corruption case to continue. They have moved a discharge application in terms of section 174 of the Criminal Procedure Act.

Legal analyst Melusi Xulu said when paraphrased, the section states that if at the end of the state's case there is no evidence upon which a reasonable court can convict the accused, the accused can be acquitted.

“It doesn't mean you know that there's no evidence, it means that evidence that is there at the end of the state's case is insufficient for a conviction.

“A very important case that we usually quote is the case of S v. Lubaba, it's a 2001 case where the court stated that if it happens at the end of the state's case there's no way a state can get a conviction unless the accused person goes to the witness box to testify in his defense and that is how they can get evidence or be able to secure a conviction and at that stage that defense should be given an acquittal.

“So at this moment the question is on the 13 charges that she has been charged with, is there sufficient evidence at this stage to say that she can be convicted? That's the question."

World.title: Uganda receives King Oyo’s remains
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The body of Uganda's King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi the Fourth has returned to the country after his death in the United States at the age of 34.

He was receiving treatment in the US for cancer.

President Yoweri Museveni received the casket at Entebbe Airport.

King Oyo became ruler of the Tooro Kingdom at the age of three following the death of his father in 1995.

He reigned for 31 years and was recognised by Guinness World Records as the world's youngest reigning monarch.

Uganda's traditional kings have mainly cultural roles with limited political powers.

King Oyo will be buried next week.

World.title: UN backs map showing Africa’s true size
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The United Nations General Assembly has adopted a resolution calling for a world map that better represents Africa's actual size.

The resolution was sponsored by Togo and supported by 164 countries including France and the United Kingdom.

The United States voted against it and six countries abstained.

The Mercator projection has been criticized for making regions near the equator appear smaller than they are.

Africa is about 14 times larger than Greenland despite the two appearing roughly the same size on the Mercator map.

The projection was created by Flemish cartographer Gerardus Mercator in 1569 for navigation.

Its distortion reflects the difficulty of representing the spherical Earth on a flat map.

World.title: Abduction trap: How weighbridge police colluded with attackers in Kiprotich's abduction
World.content:
Standard Group Associate Editor Alex Kiprotich was abducted by state operatives along the Gilgil–Nakuru Road on August 01, 2026.

Barely 100 meters away from the Gilgil weighbridge station in Nakuru, where police stand guard in the full glare of six CCTV cameras, Standard Group Associate Editor Alex Kiprotich and his driver Geoffrey Kamau lived through one of the most chilling experiences of their lives.

In a dramatic scene that continues to raise questions about the safety of everyday Kenyans, armed men ambushed their vehicle at a strategic choke point along the busy highway.

World.title: Sifuna condemns abduction of Standard Group Associate Editor
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Busia County Senator Okiya Omtata, Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna, Bumula MP Jack Wamboka during the burial service of Mary Gorreti Okiya at Kabula, in Bumula on September 5,2026. [Benjamin Sakwa, Standard]

Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna has declared that the fight to restore democracy, media freedom and the rule of law following the abduction of Standard Group Senior Editor will form the centrepiece of the Linda Mwananchi government vowing to defeat President William Ruto in the 2027 General Election.

Sifuna accused President Ruto’s administration of undermining constitutional freedoms and creating an atmosphere of fear, saying the country must be returned to what he described as “the rail of the six important values” enshrined in the Constitution.

Speaking in Bumula Constituency, Kakamega County during the burial of Mary Goreti, the sister of Busia Senator Okiya Omtatah, Sifuna strongly condemned the abduction and arrest of a Standard Group Associate Editor, Alex Kiprotich, arguing that journalists must be protected if Kenya is to remain a democratic country.

“It is impossible that you are driving on the road and you are taken away the way the way the Standard Group Journaliat and Editor Alex Kiprotich was taken. Kenyans want to live in a free country. We do not want to live in fear,” said Sifuna.

He questioned the circumstances surrounding the incident and accused the Government of failing to protect media freedom, adding that the Linda Mwananchi movement would seek to restore institutions and constitutional safeguards if elected to power, arguing that democracy could not survive where citizens, journalists and political opponents lived in fear.

"You cannot just arrest a senior journalist in the middle of the road with police carrying firearms, then you dump him some 500kilometres near the dam, a country cannot have democracy if media is not being respected and allowed to do it's work as per the constitution," said Sifuna.

He said the movement’s agenda was not merely about removing the current administration from power but it's main plan is rebuilding systems of governance around constitutionalism, democracy, individual freedoms and the rule of law.

“With less than 11 months remaining, we want to tell Kenyans that our entire plan is to return this country to the rails of the six important values contained in our Constitution, including democracy, freedom of citizens and the rule of law,” said Sifuna.

Sifuna also accused the Government of using threats against political opponents, saying leaders should not threaten citizens with arrest, expulsion or other forms of intimidation.

He challenged religious leaders to remind politicians that the power to determine the length of a person's life belongs to God.

Sifuna further linked the rule of law to economic growth, warning that investors would be reluctant to establish businesses in Kenya if government could arbitrarily order them to leave.

He said Kenya could not rely on government alone to create employment for millions of young people, arguing that the country needed both local and foreign investors.

“No investor can bring his project to a country where he can wake up one day and the President tells him, ‘Pack and go.’ It is impossible,” Sifuna said.

He argued that investor confidence was also affected by the possibility of commercial disputes being referred to foreign jurisdictions because investors lacked confidence in Kenya’s legal system.

Sifuna also criticised the government over the ongoing nurses and midwives strike, saying the rule of law required the State to honour agreements signed with workers.

World.title: Murkomen reaffirms IG Kanja's command of National Police Service
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Interior Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen has reaffirmed that the Inspector General of Police retains constitutional command of the National Police Service, saying the government will continue to respect the independence of the office.

Speaking during the passing-out parade of new Administration Police recruits in Nairobi, Murkomen said the Inspector General has authority over key operational matters within the service, including investigations, promotions and deployment of officers.

“Your Excellency, the Inspector General of Police retains the command of the National Police Service, especially on matters of investigation, promotion and deployment of officers without interference from anyone, including the Cabinet Secretary. We will continue respecting Article 245 of the Constitution,” Murkomen said.

His remarks come amid public debate over the relationship between the Interior Ministry and the National Police Service, particularly allegations that political leaders sometimes issue direct instructions to police officers.

Murkomen dismissed criticism directed at the office of the Inspector General, describing some of its proponents as tribalists and propagandists. He maintained that the Inspector General is carrying out his responsibilities and said he had confidence in the leadership of the police service.

“I have full faith in the IG and believe that every act that is done by the National Police Service is guided by the Constitution,” he said.

The Cabinet Secretary also addressed concerns over his role in directing the police, saying that his responsibility is primarily to provide policy direction rather than interfere with the operational command of the service.

“When required to give policy direction, I always give it in writing and we will continue to support the independence of the National Police Service from external interference,” Murkomen said.

During the ceremony, Murkomen also cautioned the newly graduated officers against corruption, excessive alcohol consumption and conduct that could undermine the reputation of the police service.

He urged the recruits to uphold discipline and protect the dignity of the police uniform, noting that the respect they receive from members of the public would depend largely on their conduct.

The Cabinet Secretary encouraged the officers to understand the responsibility that comes with joining the National Police Service and to discharge their duties within the confines of the Constitution and the law.

The passing-out ceremony marked the entry of the new recruits into the police service that made the CS use the occasion to emphasize professional conduct and respect for the constitutional framework governing policing in Kenya.

World.title: Ruto assures Kajiado residents of full control of Amboseli National Park
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto inspects the Rombo Clusters Irrigation Development Project in Kajiado County on September 3, 2026. [Peterson Githaiga, Standard]

President William Ruto has assured Kajiado residents that they will soon have full control of the management of Amboseli National Park, following his decision to return the park to the county in November 2025.

However, he said the transfer has been temporarily halted by the court.

The President hit out at those he accused of frustrating the move, saying they will be in for a rude shock.

“They took us to court over the Social Health Authority and the Affordable Housing Programme, but these programmes are progressing well. Similarly, I want to assure the people of Kajiado that, before the end of this year, Amboseli will be fully in the hands of Kajiado County,” he said.

Speaking in Kajiado County on Thursday during his development tour, President Ruto reiterated that he will not relent in his pursuit of equity and inclusive development across Kenya, saying that longstanding inequalities have unduly benefited certain regions at the expense of others.

He revealed that the securitisation of the Road Maintenance Levy Fund and the Sports Fund has enabled the Government to clear pending bills in the roads sector and construct 6,000km of new roads, and accelerate the construction of 32 new stadia across the country.

"The Road Maintenance Levy Fund was misused to only build roads in some parts of the country. Those opposing securitisation are unhappy that we are advancing equity," he said.

The President began his tour at Oloirien in Kajiado South Constituency by inspecting progress of the 67km Illasit-Rombo-Chala-Njukini-Taveta road, which is 48 per cent completed.

The Sh9.4 billion project will cut travel time between Kajiado and Taita-Taveta counties from two hours to just 40 minutes, thus easing the movement of goods and people.

The Head of State announced that eight new roads of 220km are being built across Kajiado County at a cost of Sh13 billion to open up the region and improve transport.

The President commissioned Sh221 million Rombo Clusters Irrigation Development Project, which is expected to enhance livelihoods and boost irrigation in the area.

He also inspected progress of the Sh2.2 billion Loitoktok Affordable Housing Project, and laid the foundation stone for the Sh220 million Loitoktok Kenya Medical Training College student hostels with a 580-bed capacity.

At Kimana, in Kajiado South Constituency, President Ruto commissioned the Sh2.7 billion Sultan Hamud-Loitoktok 132kV Transmission Line and Loitoktok Sub-Station, which will serve the residents of Kajiado South and parts of Makueni County.

He inspected construction of the Kimana modern market, which is aimed at giving traders dignified working environment.

At Namanga, Kajiado Central Constituency, the President commissioned the Namanga Sub-Station, a project of the Kenya Electricity Transmission Company (KETRACO), which is part of the 132KV Machakos- Konza-Isinya-Namanga Transmission Project.

Namanga Modern Market, which is under construction at a cost of Sh50 million, will benefit 120 traders at the border town.

In Kajiado town, the President toured the construction of the Kajiado Affordable Housing Project, a Sh473 million investment that will deliver 196 housing units, as well as the 100-unit police housing project at a cost of Sh137 million.

He also inspected the progress of the 580-bed student hostels at Maasai National Polytechnic, which is being built at a cost of KSh216 million.

Ruto ordered the closer of Tata Chemicals, saying the government will identify a new and responsible investor to take over soda ash mining operations at Lake Magadi.

The President said Tata Chemicals had failed to adequately modernise the plant, create sufficient employment opportunities for residents, and deliver meaningful economic benefits to the people of Kenya.

“It is unfair for one company to dominate the ownership and operations of Magadi Soda for years, yet it has done little to improve the factory or create employment opportunities for our youth,” he said at Rombo in Kajiado South Constituency.

He added: “Because they have been unable to do anything meaningful with the plant for more than 100 years, I have directed them to pack up and go.”

The Ministry of Mining suspended the company’s mining operations in July 2026 over concerns relating to regulatory compliance, value addition and licensing.

The ministry also ordered the closure of the company’s depot in Kajiado Town for contravening environmental regulations.

In addition, the company has been unable to reach an agreement with the Kajiado County Government over a land rates dispute following the expiry of its operating licence in 2023.

The plant produces soda ash, or sodium carbonate, a key industrial mineral used in the manufacture of glass, soap and laundry detergents, among other products.

Despite being Africa’s largest soda ash producer, President Ruto noted that the operation had not delivered commensurate benefits to Kenyans over its more than 100-year history, particularly because much of the soda ash produced is exported for processing and consumption in overseas markets.

The Government, the President said, would therefore prioritise an investor capable of modernising the facility, expanding local value addition, creating jobs for young people, and ensuring that Kenya derives greater economic value from its natural resources.

World.title: IG Kanja orders probe into abduction of Standard Group Associate Editor
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Standard Group PLC Associate Editor Alex Kiprotich. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

The Inspector General of Police Douglas Kanja has ordered immediate and transparent investigations into the alleged abduction of Standard Group Associate Editor Alex Kiprotich in Gilgil.

The National Police Service (NPS) said it had taken note of reports that Kiprotich was allegedly kidnapped on Tuesday and had moved swiftly to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident.

NPS spokesperson Muchiri Nyaga said the police service treats kidnapping and abduction with the utmost seriousness, describing the offences as a threat to the lives, liberty and security of Kenyans.

“The Inspector General of Police has accordingly ordered immediate investigations to determine what transpired, including the identity of the heavily armed individuals reportedly seen ordering occupants out of their vehicle,” Nyaga said in a statement.

The NPS said its Anti-Abduction Unit, established to investigate abductions and disappearances, had taken up the matter and would work to ensure that those responsible are brought to justice.

“We unequivocally condemn any act of kidnapping, abduction, or intimidation intended to interfere with press freedom or any other constitutional right,” Nyaga said.

The police service assured the public that the investigation into the Gilgil incident would be conducted transparently, stressing that no one was above the law.

The development comes amid growing condemnation of Kiprotich’s alleged abduction, with the Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) also calling for an immediate investigation.

CPJ Africa Director Angela Quintal described the incident as a “shameful indictment” of the Kenya Kwanza administration, raising concerns over the safety of journalists and press freedom in the country.

“The attempt to forcibly disappear Alex Kiprotich, three days after President William Ruto railed against The Standard Group, reflects the growing dangers that journalists face in Kenya, despite the president’s earlier promise to allow the press to work freely,” Quintal said.

The New York-based press freedom organisation further expressed concern over what it described as an escalation in cases of abductions and enforced disappearances in Kenya.

World.title: Trumpets of reforms blow louder as Kenya marks 16 years under 2010 Constitution
World.content:
The Constitution, Kenyan flag and the National anthem. [PCS]

On Thursday, August 27, a group of people largely composed of the youth gathered under some trees at Jeevanjee Gardens in Nairobi, carrying Kenyans flag, and banners and placards inscribed with "implement the constitution. Kenyans first" words.

These were in protests against what they believed is deliberate failure of those in authority to fully implement the 2010 Constitution.

World.title: Ruto allies hit back at Gachagua over IEBC tender concerns
World.content:
The Kenya Integrated Elections Management System (KIEMS) kit. [File, Standard]

President William Ruto’s allies led by National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang’ula have launched a scathing attack on former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua and the Opposition over their criticism of the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC), citing blackmail by the Opposition.

The leaders warned that attempts by politicians to dictate how the electoral agency procures technology and other election materials could undermine public confidence in the 2027 General Election.

World.title: IEBC rejects Gachagua's claims, defends 2027 polls preparations
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

IEBC dismissed Gachagua's claims of political interference, graft and voter suppression in 2027 polls.

The Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) has dismissed allegations of political interference, corruption and voter suppression surrounding preparations for the 2027 General Election, terming the claims false, unsubstantiated and aimed at undermining public confidence in the electoral body.

In a statement issued on Thursday, IEBC Chairperson Erastus Edung Ethekon said the allegations followed statements made by Democracy for Citizens Party (DCP) leader Rigathi Gachagua during a press briefing on Wednesday.

The commission specifically rejected claims that politicians had purchased a house for its chairperson to influence him, saying the allegation had changed from an alleged Sh80 million property to one worth Sh200 million.

"The allegations that a house has been purchased for the Chairperson of IEBC by some politicians for purposes of influencing him are unfortunate, unfair and unsubstantiated to date," Ethekon stated.

The commission also challenged Gachagua to provide evidence, including the location of the property, sale and transfer documents, payment receipts and details of the parties involved, and submit them to the Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission for investigation.

The electoral body also dismissed claims of improper staff changes, saying deployment and redeployment of employees was part of its normal administrative functions and was guided by its human resource policies and public service regulations.

"The Commission complies with its Human Resource policies, guidelines and other relevant instruments under the larger public service when engaging employees," the statement read in part.

It further denied allegations of malpractice against the chairperson and vice-chairperson, describing them as fabricated claims intended to damage the reputation of the commissioners and the commission.

Magarini by-election

On the Magarini by-election, IEBC said the poll was conducted in a free, fair and credible manner and was not challenged through an election petition. The commission added that it had successfully conducted several by-elections and was prepared to oversee the 2027 General Election.

At the same time, IEBC also defended its procurement process for election technology and ballot papers, saying all tenders were being conducted in accordance with Chapter 12 of the Constitution and the Public Procurement and Asset Disposal Act, 2015.

"Two key tenders, one for the Integrated Elections Management System, hardware and accessories, and another for ballot papers and other election materials, have temporarily been halted following a request for review filed before the Public Procurement Administrative Review Board," IEBC stated.

According to IEBC, documents for the technology tender were uploaded on its website and the Public Procurement Information Portal on August 11, 2026.

The commission said the technical specifications were generic and performance-based and open to all qualified suppliers. It stressed that the procurement process was still at its initial stages and that no company had been awarded the tender.

Voter register protected

The commission also dismissed claims that voter registration data could be manipulated or shared with external parties, insisting that the Register of Voters remained under its exclusive custody.

"Voter registration involves several stages, including in-person registration, verification of identity, collection of biometric and biographical data, transmission to a central database and automated biometric deduplication," IEBC added.

Flagged records are subjected to data cleaning, validation and adjudication before valid records are incorporated into the register.

The register will subsequently undergo a 30-day biometric verification exercise, followed by an independent audit before it is finalised and certified for use in an election.

IEBC said allegations of bribery, predetermined tender awards and voter suppression were false and potentially harmful to public confidence in the electoral process.

World.title: Egypt penalizes school administrators over false niqab mandate rumors
World.content:
Egypt’s Ministry of Education and Technical Education has clarified that a social media post claiming a mandatory face veil policy at Nagaa Said Preparatory Co-educational School in Dishna, Qena Governorate, was published in error and promptly removed.

The ministry confirmed that the school principal and the Facebook page administrator have been referred to legal affairs for necessary disciplinary action regarding the incident.

Addressing an accompanying photograph that showed all female students wearing the niqab, the ministry revealed that the image was fake and generated using artificial intelligence (AI) technology, and did not reflect actual school environment or student body.

Officials reiterated that all schools nationwide remain bound by Ministerial Decree #167 of 2023, which regulates standardized school uniform specifications across both public and private institutions.

The ministry emphasized that official school social media pages must strictly reflect educational guidelines and policies with precision and accountability.

This move aims to regulate content published across official school channels, curb the spread of inaccurate information, and ensure administrative compliance across all educational institutions.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Naglaa Fathi – The eternal sweetheart
World.content:
Egyptian screen icon Naglaa Fathi long epitomized unfiltered grace, maintaining the same untouched, youthful spirit that defined her breakthrough decades ago without relying on cosmetic enhancements or synthetic alterings.

Known off-screen by her birth name, Fatma al-Zahraa, the legendary actress endured a series of personal and health hardships over the past decade and a half.

Chief among them was a battle against a severe, rare form of psoriasis—a medical trial she met with remarkable resilience.

Fathi agreed to participate in European clinical trials for an experimental treatment, effectively acting as a pioneer whose successful recovery helped pave the way for other patients suffering from the condition.

However, her victory over the illness coincided with public controversy. Following media backlash and false reports surrounding state funding for her costly medical care overseas, Fathi and her late husband, renowned journalist Hamdi Qandil, publicly clarified that they personally financed the entire treatment protocol.

While self-funding her care, Fathi expressed deep appreciation for the Egyptian state’s moral support throughout her medical journey.

Fathi lost her husband, soulmate, and legendary journalist Hamdi Qandil eight years ago, entering a period of deep personal bereavement.

Her dedication to preserving his memory captured public attention when a viral photograph showed the veteran actress standing resolutely outside her Heliopolis residence.

Fathi stood beneath a newly restored plaque from the National Organization for Urban Harmony’s “Lived Here” memorial initiative, which honors Egypt’s cultural and intellectual luminaries.

The moment followed a high-profile incident in which thieves targeted the building entrance and stole the original brass commemorative marker honoring Qandil.

Refusing to let his tribute be erased, Fathi petitioned cultural authorities and pushed until the official memorial plaque was reinstalled at the doorstep of their longtime home.

Fathi is now experiencing deep sorrow following the loss of her only daughter, Yasmine, whose recent funeral service at the mosque saw chaotic media scenes.

In response, the family—specifically Yasmine’s father, Saif Abol Naga—decided to prohibit all photography and filming at the condolence service.

I hope her request is respected by everyone.

Fathi originally stepped away from acting studios in 2000, though she did not view the move as the end of her artistic career.

She pursued several projects, including a self-produced film intended to co-star Omar Sharif and be directed by Samah Anwar, who had formally studied filmmaking.

Despite holding multiple working sessions together, creative differences arose between Fathi and Sharif, halting communication and bringing the project to a complete standstill. Subsequent project offers failed to spark her interest.

Years ago, several websites published a recent photograph of the veteran actress.

Some expected the image to provoke sadness among observers tracing the effects of time, seemingly preferring she resemble certain older female stars whose faces appear decades younger through artificial means.

Contrary to those expectations, the photograph brought happiness to millions.

Fathi stepped away from public life in a quiet manner that reflects her personality—one that avoids noise and stays clear of any battle outside the artistic realm.

Over the course of her long artistic journey, Fathi frequently served on festival jury panels, demonstrating a sharp capacity for technical film analysis alongside her signature wit and quick intellect.

During daily gatherings alongside her late husband, renowned journalist Hamdi Qandil—in Cairo and Dubai while he hosted his widely viewed weekly show “Qalam Rasas” on Dubai TV—an agreement was forged to document Fathi’s life story across a 30-episode television program directed by Ali Badrakhan.

Initial structural planning for the series had already commenced, relying heavily on Fathi’s candor, humor, and extensive cinematic legacy.

However, the project was ultimately shelved before completion. The author refrained from pressing Fathi for an explanation, recognizing that as the originator of the idea, she maintained full discretion to withdraw from its execution.

Over the past decade, Fathi tightly closed her personal circle, limiting phone calls to a very small group of family and close friends. Respecting her decision, the author refrained from reaching out to avoid obligating her to respond.

Numerous film festivals both inside Egypt and abroad attempted to honor Fathi, but she firmly closed the door on public tributes. She has never denied her historic career—studded with dozens of artistic and social achievements—including humanitarian work that she consistently preferred to keep out of the spotlight.

Fathi is currently living through the peak of grief following the death of Yasmine, who was always the apple of her eye.

With unwavering faith in God and the warmth of love from millions of fans, Fathi continues to draw strength, carrying Yasmine’s memory deep within her heart.

Author’s biography:

Tarek al-Shenawy is a journalist, film critic, and professor of film criticism at the Faculty of Mass Communication, Cairo University.

He holds a Bachelor’s degree from the Faculty of Mass Communication in Cairo University, and a Bachelor’s degree from the Institute of Cinema.

Shenawy has won numerous awards for best critical article from the Syndicate of Journalists multiple times, as well as from film societies. He was awarded the title of Best Popular Film Critic by the “Der Giest” Association in 2015 – a title that has not been awarded to anyone since.

He has also chaired and participated in the judging committees of numerous international film festivals, including the Valencia and Dubai Film Festivals.

He began practicing film criticism nearly 35 years ago in the Rose al-Yousse magazine and continues to write a weekly column titled “Kalma we Nos” (Word and a Half) on its pages. He has written for numerous magazines, newspapers, and websites both inside and outside Egypt.

He currently writes a daily column in Al-Masry Al-Youm newspaper and a weekly column in Al-Sharq al-Awsat newspaper, and has published over thirty books.

World.title: 24 hours that show how preoccupied Trump is
World.content:
It can be difficult to decide which Roman metaphor more aptly captures President Donald Trump’s posture these days.

Is it “bread and circuses,” feeding the American people a series of distractions — amusing or otherwise — from their worries about the economy? Or is it Nero, fiddling with his ballroom plans while the Republican Party’s midterm hopes burn?

What’s clear is that Trump and his administration aren’t going to course correct any time soon.

The last 24 hours have been a case in point. And the last couple weeks have been inauspicious for anyone who hoped Trump might suddenly focus on the political task at hand.

Thursday marked exactly two months until Election Day 2026. And the first votes are about to be cast, with North Carolina sending out mail ballots on Friday.

But despite a bevy of polling showing Americans want Trump to focus on affordability and the economy, he appears preoccupied with anything but.

On Thursday alone, we learned the Trump administration has hired a new pool contractor to clean up the mess he made of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, announced the start of construction on Trump’s 250-foot “triumphal arch” and launched a series of arcade-style video games, including one that allows users to arrest undocumented immigrants.

The White House is also reportedly launching a reality show-like competition for entrepreneurs, just weeks after Trump’s “Patriot Games” flopped and after an actual reality show from the Department of Transportation was released. (It says a nonprofit paid for it; not taxpayers.)

By Friday morning, two big stories — from the New Yorker and New York Magazine — detailed what can only be called Trump’s obsession with his ballroom and other construction and beautification projects in Washington, DC.

Trump even sat for an interview — and gave a construction tour, of course — for the New York Magazine piece.

Reporter Ben Terris reported that the president’s official calendar is “peppered with meetings about other projects around Washington that can often last an hour or longer.”

And in perhaps the most eyebrow-raising scene, Trump actually agrees with Georgia Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff’s contention that he’s building monuments to himself because he doesn’t think others can be counted on to do it.

“That’s true,” Trump said. “Nobody will do it once I’m gone. When I leave here, nobody will.”

The fact that Trump would say this out loud is stunning. Ossoff meant this as a dig.

But it also suggests Trump might be feeling the pressure to get these projects done fast. He has a finite amount of time to plaster his name on things and build things that he’ll be remembered by. It could get more difficult by January, when Democrats could control one or both chambers of Congress.

Trump even talks about how it will supposedly be impossible for Democrats to demolish his ballroom, if they wanted to. (“It’s nuclear concrete,” he told New York Magazine. “I think it would be very hard. It’s meant for if there’s a nuclear attack.”)

Terris also runs through how Trump in his public appearances often seems distracted by his construction projects as he’s attending to much more serious business.

And that’s really the problem with all of this, at least if you’re a congressional Republican staring at a concerning midterm election.

It’s not just that Trump is distracted; it’s that he’s focused on things that polls show Americans view as frivolous and don’t want — at the expense of things they really want him to do (i.e. lowering prices and ending the war with Iran).

Trump’s ballroom is 2-to-1 unpopular.

Americans opposed his 250-foot “triumphal arch” 52%-21% in an April poll.

A July poll showed 65% of Americans described themselves as upset or dissatisfied with the ballroom, arch and Reflecting Pool projects.

While Trump tries to put his name on things like the Kennedy Center, just 9% of Americans think that’s appropriate for him to do as an incumbent president.

And Trump’s other preoccupation in recent days and weeks — his new trade war with Canada, which led him move to rename Lake Ontario as “Lake America” — fares little better. Reuters-Ipsos polling this week showed Americans opposed the Canada tariffs 57%-20% and the “Lake America” renaming 63%-14%.

Trump last week held a White House event for the latter move, which it turns out even his fellow Republicans oppose by double digits.

All of this cements a tough picture for the GOP. Polling has for months shown that Americans view Trump as neglecting more important fare.

CBS News polling has recently shown 78% of Americans said he’s not focused enough on lowering prices, and July CNN polling shows around the same percentage (73%) said he hasn’t paid enough attention to the country’s most important problems.

It’s not fair to say Trump has completely neglected the cost of living.

He recently announced he would pause tariffs on imported beef to try to lower prices for consumers, and on Friday he threatened to stop trading with other countries if the Federal Reserve doesn’t lower interest rates.

Both moves could theoretically save people money.

But both moves also betray Trump’s preference for questionable quick fixes. The beef tariffs move, for example, is expected to have a negligible impact, CNN reported, while irritating domestic cattle ranchers and even some Republicans. And the extortionate threat to the Fed seems unlikely to bear fruit. (Indeed, lowering interest rates could actually send inflation higher.)

The CNN poll in July contained another telling finding. Fully 66% of Americans said Trump did not put the good of the country above his own personal gain. That included 76% of independents and 30% of Republicans.

And more than a month later, with the 2026 general election truly kicking off, it’s as if he’s bent on proving those people right.

World.title: US oil deal promises a flood of investment in Venezuela. When will its people feel the benefits?
World.content:
The enormous investments that the US and Venezuela have promised from their new oil production deal have brought cautious optimism that Venezuelans face a new period of prosperity after more than a decade of economic and social turmoil.
